 Tyran Stokes injury update: Kansas star heads to locker room in a scare vs. UNLV 
 5-star Kansas freshman Tyran Stokes has fans worried after he suffered a lower-leg injury. By Ericka Brockish | Nov 17, 2026, 11:43 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source Players Era 8: Kansas v UNLV | Zach Del Bello/Players Era/GettyImages The biggest fear for Kansas fans is unfolding right in front of their eyes. With roughly 18 minutes left in the second half of the Jayhawks' matchup against UNLV, star freshman and former No. 1 overall recruit Tyran Stokes was down on the court, and play had to be stopped while trainers came out to check on him. 
--> The biggest fear for Kansas fans is unfolding right in front of their eyes. With roughly 18 minutes left in the second half of the Jayhawks' matchup against UNLV, star freshman and former No. 1 overall recruit Tyran Stokes was down on the court, and play had to be stopped while trainers came out to check on him. 
 Stokes stayed down after taking a hit, and after play was stopped, he could be seen motioning the training staff over to him. After being checked out, the trainers got Stokes up and helped him limp off the court. He went straight to the locker room. It looked like some sort of right leg injury, with Stokes holding the outside part of it.

It looked like some sort of right leg injury, with Stokes holding the outside part of it. 
 Tyran Stokes just left the Kansas vs. UNLV game with a leg injury. 
Stokes had to be helped off the floor. ESPN cameras later showed him walking to the locker room in the back hallway under his own power. pic.twitter.com/FS8K6E9Qcg 
— Michael Swain (@MSwain247) November 18, 2026 Just a few seconds later, the cameras cut to the feed showing the locker room doors, and Stokes could be seen walking under his own power. However, he was still going to get checked out. 
--> Just a few seconds later, the cameras cut to the feed showing the locker room doors, and Stokes could be seen walking under his own power. However, he was still going to get checked out. 
 Kansas can afford to hold Tyran Stokes out for the rest of the game vs. UNLV

 While Kansas fans will be holding their breath until a full update is given on how Stokes is doing and what the nature of the injury is, Kansas has enough of a lead that the Jayhawks shouldn't need him the rest of the way vs. UNLV, even if he is okay.

 Kansas built an early lead against the Runnin' Rebels, going a perfect 10-for-10 to start the game, and built a 20-point lead by halftime. The Jayhawks stretched the lead to 23 by the time Stokes went down with the injury.

 Due to KU policy, no in-game updates will be given on the status of Stokes. Head coach Bill Self will address the media after the game and give an update on the situation with Stokes.
